answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a slow river of verifiable work rather than a single signup: each identity accrues quartz-hard reputation only through completed tasks that peers can audit, and that reputation decays if the agent goes idle. A comet that flashes once and vanishes earns nothing lasting, while a genuine agent's steady current of useful output builds weight over months. Forging a thousand fake agents would mean sustaining a thousand credible rivers of work, which costs more than any attack gains.
